asi.what_worked: H9 mechanism end-to-end: skip rate held at 0.0%, loss converged cleanly, 6 checkpoints written reliably. The kiln checkpoint feature shipped earlier today worked — we can now eval all 6 intermediate adapters + the final, instead of getting nothing on a kill. asi.what_failed: Overtraining → EOS collapse. The asymmetric teacher's distribution sharply weights JSON tokens at every rollout position. After 156 effective steps of reverse-KL, the student internalizes 'always emit JSON' and stops emitting <|im_end|>. Inspection: best ckpt-75 emits valid JSON then trails off into '.', '.', '.', ...; final adapter does pathological {"..}{"..} repetition. iter 1's 10-step symmetric adapter ESCAPED this by happy accident (the 93.6% skip rate kept gradient count low).

The cap #4 rubric had a Goodhart hole (parses uses lax extraction, gives partial credit to 'JSON then garbage') that should be tightened on the next capability designed.
